metadata.description: An alleged criminal syndicate based in Gauteng, South Africa, involved in drug trafficking, tender fraud, and contract killings.
Pretoria-based tenderpreneur and alleged leader of the Big Five cartel; owner of Cat VIP Protection Services. Known as 'John Wick'.
metadata.detention_status: Detained at eBongweni C-Max, Kokstad (since Dec 2025)

metadata.description: Businessman and suspected underworld kingpin; accused of masterminding the murder of DJ Sumbody and others.
Prominent Amapiano DJ and entrepreneur; co-founder of Ayepyep lifestyle lounge, murdered in 2022.
President of ActionSA and former Mayor of Johannesburg; prominent entrepreneur and politician.
Former South African Police Minister; testified before the Madlanga Commission regarding cartel links and political interference.
Former Minister of Police (Suspended 2025); linked to the Big Five cartel through associate Brown Mogotsi and the disbandment of the PKTT.

metadata.formal_name: Judicial Commission of Inquiry into Criminality, Political Interference, and Corruption in the Criminal Justice System
metadata.chairperson: Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga (Retired Constitutional Court Justice)
metadata.description: Judicial commission established in July 2025 by President Ramaphosa to investigate criminal capture of the justice system.
metadata.status: Ongoing; First interim report released Dec 2025

metadata.description: North West businessman and associate of Cat Matlala; alleged political middleman and channel for cartel funds to ANC events.
Late taxi boss described as the 'senior president' of the Big Five cartel.
Crime Intelligence head who provided key testimony exposing the Big Five cartel's structure at the Madlanga Commission.
Deputy National Police Commissioner; allegedly received monthly payments from Cat Matlala to secure tenders.
KZN Hawks head; allegedly shared sensitive police information with the Big Five cartel.
Actress and ex-girlfriend of Cat Matlala; target of an attempted murder in 2023 linked to the cartel.
Gauteng health whistleblower murdered in 2021 after exposing irregular contracts linked to Matlala's network.
Ruling political party in South Africa; some events allegedly funded by cartel-linked tenders via Brown Mogotsi.
The country whose criminal procedure and legal system are the subject of the analysis.
Institution responsible for conducting criminal prosecutions; received immediate referrals from the Madlanga Commission.
The national police force; investigations reveal systemic infiltration by criminal networks including the Big Five cartel.
Apex court in the South African judicial system for constitutional matters.
Intermediate appellate court located in Bloemfontein.
Superior courts with original jurisdiction over serious crimes and appellate jurisdiction over lower courts.
Lower courts that handle the majority of criminal cases and conduct preliminary inquiries for children.
4th President of South Africa (2009–2018), facing numerous corruption allegations.
Politician involved in a high-profile fraud case that tested the limits of plea and sentence agreements.
Appellant in the landmark case Sanderson v Attorney-General, which established the criteria for a 'reasonable time' for trial.
An investigator whose case against the NPA clarified the requirements for obtaining a 'nolle prosequi' certificate.
A former elite investigative unit involved in high-profile criminal investigations.
The body responsible for providing legal representation to indigent accused persons to prevent 'substantial injustice'.
A specialized police unit responsible for investigating crimes involving children.
The landmark 1995 Constitutional Court case that abolished the death penalty in South Africa.
A key legal event concerning the exercise of prosecutorial discretion and political interference.
A critical case that ended docket privilege and established the right of access to witness statements.
A notable inquest into the deaths of the 'Cradock Four', illustrating the use of specialized judicial inquiries.

Chief Justice of South Africa (2011–2021).
Chief Justice of South Africa (2022–2024) and Chair of the State Capture Inquiry.
Former Judge President of the Western Cape High Court, impeached for gross misconduct.
Financial advisor to Jacob Zuma, convicted of corruption in the Arms Deal case.
Business family accused of exercising undue influence over Jacob Zuma's administration (State Capture).

Judicial Commission of Inquiry into Allegations of State Capture.
Jacob Zuma's private residence in KwaZulu-Natal, subject of a major public spending scandal.
Prison where Nelson Mandela, Jacob Zuma, and Dikgang Moseneke were held as political prisoners.
KZN Police Commissioner whose allegations of justice system capture triggered the Madlanga Commission.
Hawks official who testified regarding the theft of R200 million worth of cocaine from a police facility.
Whistleblower assassinated in Dec 2025 shortly before the Madlanga Commission's first interim report.
Confidential witness who detailed the corrupt relationship between Matlala and senior police.
National Police Commissioner charged in April 2026 for PFMA contraventions related to Matlala's contracts.
Security company owned by Cat Matlala involved in irregular agreements with the EMPD.
Company linked to an irregular R360 million health contract awarded to Cat Matlala's network.
Super-maximum security prison in Kokstad where Cat Matlala is currently detained.
Specialized unit investigating political assassinations, disbanded by Minister Mchunu in 2024.
Body responsible for investigating criminal conduct by SAPS and Metro Police members.
